asof: Settles Wed 4 Nov 2026 · written Thu 5 Nov
headline: Democratic sweep and oil slump rally reds and greens 5.5–7bp, Z6 unchanged; U7 peak at 4.50% still prices about two hikes.
summary: The strip bull-flattened on Wednesday: Z6 and U6 were unchanged at 4.16% and 3.925% and H7 fell 1.5bp to 4.355%, while M7 and U7 dropped 3.5bp and 4.5bp to 4.47% and 4.50%, and Z7 through Z9 led with 5.5–7bp declines. That reversed Tuesday's selloff past the March contract: month-to-date Z6 is 1.5bp higher and H7 flat, but M7 through Z9 are 1–4.5bp lower. The peak is still SR3U7 at 4.50%, now 53bp over the 3.97% SOFR fixing, with 15bp of easing priced from there to Z9. That is still about one hike more than the Fed's September projections, which showed one more move this year, and the consensus call of a December hike.
drivers: Democratic sweep and an oil slump pull 2027 hikes lower

Democrats took both the House and the Senate, and WTI fell about 7–8% into the high $80s while Brent traded below $100 for the first time since 7 October, on hopes the result speeds an end to the Iran war. One-year inflation swaps dropped to about 2.1% from 2.4% on Tuesday, and the 2-year yield hit a two-month low of 4.546% from 4.612%. In SR3, M7 fell 3.5bp, U7 4.5bp and H8 through Z9 6–7bp.

Treasury kept coupon sizes unchanged, selling $125bn of 3-, 10- and 30-year debt next week to raise about $28bn of new cash, and dropped 'at least' from its 'next several quarters' guidance, which Bloomberg reads as opening the door to long-end cuts in 2027. The 7-year moves to a quarterly new issue. Supply relief helped the reds: Z6/Z7 tightened 5.5bp to +31bp.
Mixed data keep the December hike priced

ADP rose 86,000 against about 75,000 expected, while ISM services slipped to 54.5 from 54.9 (54.8 expected), with new orders down to 55.9 from 59.8 and prices paid still high at 73.0. Firm hiring and sticky prices kept the front anchored: Z6 was unchanged at 4.16%, so the whole move came from 2027 onward.
Repo stays above the reserves rate

SOFR fixed at 3.97% on 3 November, up 2bp, 9bp over the 3.88% EFFR, above the 3.90% interest on reserves and only 3bp under the 4.00% standing repo rate. U6 at 3.925% implied, unchanged, still sits 4.5bp under the fixing.
spreads: The curve bull-flattened from H7 out, with the inversion past the peak deepening slightly. U6/Z6 held at +23.5bp (+1.25bp on the month), Z6/H7 narrowed 1.5bp to +19.5bp, H7/M7 2bp to +11.5bp and M7/U7 1bp to +3bp, while U7/Z7 fell 1bp to −3bp, so the peak stays in U7. Z6/Z7 tightened 5.5bp to +31bp (−4bp on the month) and Z6/M7 3.5bp to +31bp (−2.5bp). Past the peak, Z7/Z8 deepened 1bp to −9bp (−1.5bp month-to-date), U7/Z8 2bp to −12bp and Z8/Z9 held at −3bp; the greens are almost flat, with U8 to Z9 consecutive spreads between −1.5bp and 0. The H7/M7/U7 fly fell 1bp to +8.5bp (flat on the month) and M7/U7/Z7 held at +6bp (−0.5bp). Week- and month-to-date changes are the same, as both run from the 30 October settle.
fed: The latest fed funds futures snapshot is Tuesday's, taken before Wednesday's rally: 18.3bp for the 9 December meeting (a 73% chance of a hike), 24.5bp by January, 37.8bp by March, 52.1bp by June and a 56bp peak by September 2027 (implied EFFR 4.44%). That is 1–1.3bp below Monday beyond December, close to the 30 October month-end (17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp, 57bp peak), well below 22.6bp, 32.5bp, 49.1bp, 69.5bp and 76.5bp on 27 October, and far below a 94bp peak at end-September. SR3 has since moved ahead of ZQ: 4.44% plus SOFR's 9bp premium over EFFR is about 4.53%, 3bp above U7 at 4.50%, while Z6 at 4.16% sits about 5.5bp under the January ZQ level plus that premium. FedWatch showed about 78% for December on Wednesday morning. The strip still prices about two more hikes against one more in the Fed's September projections; Hammack dissented for a hike in October and Logan wants at least two, so payrolls on Friday (about 59,000–65,000 expected) and CPI on 10 November remain the tests.

ideas.title: Sell the Z6/M7 calendar spread (fade 2027 hikes)
ideas.why: Open and 7bp in favour at +31bp after tightening 3.5bp on Wednesday, as M7 fell 3.5bp in rate while Z6 was unchanged. The stop is trailed to +36bp to lock in part of the gain; with 11bp to target and 5bp to the stop, reward is about 2.2 times risk. Kept: the ZQ peak is 56bp against 94bp at end-September, and cheaper oil plus a Congress less likely to add fiscal stimulus weaken the case for 2027 hikes.
ideas.risk: A strong payrolls print on Friday or a hot CPI on 10 November could lift 2027 hikes again and push the spread back toward +36bp.

ideas.title: Buy 2028 easing: sell Z7, buy Z8
ideas.why: Open and 1bp in favour at −9bp, as Z8 fell 6.5bp in implied rate against 5.5bp for Z7. Only 12bp of easing is priced from Z7 to Z9; with 16bp to target and the stop tightened to +1bp, 10bp away, reward is about 1.6 times risk. Kept at about half the core size: an oil-led fall in inflation expectations should eventually pull 2028 rates under the 2027 peak.
ideas.risk: If oil rebounds on a breakdown in US–Iran talks, or term premium rises with deficits, the reds can flatten toward zero and push the spread through the stop.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through payrolls and refunding settlement

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 settled unchanged at 3.925% implied, while the latest 3.97% SOFR fixing sits 4.5bp above it, above the 3.90% interest on reserves and 3bp under the 4.00% standing repo rate. Next week's refunding auctions settle on 16 November and add about $28bn of new cash, which could keep repo firm, and only U6's final week sees the December decision; revisit after that settlement.
ideas.risk: If funding pressure fades quickly, SOFR could drop back to 3.88–3.90% and leave a few bp on the table.

Brent fell below $100 on peace hopes; a deal would pull 2027 hikes lower, a breakdown would push them back up.

The last CPI before the December meeting after 3.7% headline in September; it sets Z6 and the December hike odds.
